sections.title: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments

rows.label: Tax test: employee or contractor (Inland Revenue)
rows.value: Generally an employee if the payer controls how and when the work is done. Indicators: must do the work personally; told what to do, when and how; paid a set rate; can get overtime or penal rates; set hours; works at the payer's premises; the payer sets the standards

rows.label: Tax guidance: Interpretation Guideline IG 16/01
rows.value: Common-law tests: intention, control, independence, fundamental (in business on their own account) and integration; leading case Bryson v Three Foot Six Ltd [2005] NZSC 34

source.title: Inland Revenue (Tax technical): Interpretation Guideline IG 16/01, Determining employment status for tax purposes (employee or independent contractor?), issued 8 March 2016, paragraphs 5-6

rows.label: Employment law: gateway test (from 21 February 2026)
rows.value: A worker is a contractor if all criteria are met: a written agreement saying they are a contractor or not an employee; free to work for others; can choose when to work or subcontract; can decline extra work; had a chance to get independent advice. Otherwise the common-law test applies

rows.label: Company tax (income tax on companies) [national]
rows.value: 28% for most companies, 17.5% for Māori authorities; GloBE multinational top-up tax up to a 15% effective rate for groups with revenue over EUR 750 million (IIR and UTPR from 2025, DIIR from 2026). Paid by companies. Income Tax Act 2007; GloBE rules added by the Taxation (Annual Rates for 2023-24, Multinational Tax, and Remedial Matters) Act 2024

source.title: Inland Revenue: Tax rates for businesses (last updated 1 April 2024)

rows.label: Branch profits tax or tax on distributed profits

source.title: Inland Revenue: Tax residency status for companies (last updated 25 June 2025)

rows.label: Self-employed contributions: ACC levies [national]
rows.value: Earners' levy 1.75% including GST on liable earnings of $50,501 to $156,641 (2026/27); Work levy by ACC classification unit (average 0.69%). Paid by self-employed people, invoiced by ACC. Accident Compensation Act 2001

source.title: Inland Revenue: Payroll Calculations & Business Rules Specification 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (24 March 2026, v1.0), section 2.1; Employer's guide IR335 (September 2026), page 16

rows.label: Contractor rules: schedular payments (withholding tax) [national]
rows.value: Standard rates 10.5% to 33% by activity, chosen rates from 10% (15% for non-residents), 45% without a notification; non-resident contractors 15%. Paid by contractors, deducted by the payer as a prepayment of income tax. Income Tax Act 2007 (schedular payments) and Tax Administration Act 1994

source.title: Inland Revenue: Payroll Calculations & Business Rules Specification 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (24 March 2026, v1.0), sections 5.14, 5.14.1, 5.14.2; Employer's guide IR335 (September 2026), pages 13, 16-17

rows.label: Simplified or presumptive regime for the self-employed
rows.value: None: self-employed people pay income tax on net profit at the individual rates through an individual return; GST registration is required above $60,000 a year

source.title: Inland Revenue: Self-employed (last updated 6 July 2026)

rows.label: Non-resident tax on employment income (PAYE) [national]
rows.value: The income tax rates (10.5% to 39%) through PAYE plus the ACC earners' levy, without the IETC; 10.5% flat for recognised seasonal workers (NSW). Paid by non-resident employees, deducted by the employer. Income Tax Act 2007; double tax agreements may exempt

source.title: Inland Revenue: Employer's guide, IR335 (September 2026), page 54 (Non-residents)

rows.label: Local council rates (property tax) [local]
rows.value: Set by each council each year on land, capital or annual value; fixed charges at most 30% of rates revenue. Paid by owners of rateable land. Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

source.title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.label: Property transfer tax or stamp duty
rows.value: None: stamp duty was abolished (residential conveyance duty in 1988, all remaining conveyance and lease duty for instruments executed after 20 May 1999)

source.title: Inland Revenue: Tax Information Bulletin Vol 11 No 5 (May/June 1999), page 4: Stamp Duty Abolished (Stamp Duty Abolition Act 1999)

rows.label: Capital gains: taxed as income in set cases (bright-line test, share sales for resale) [national]
rows.value: No separate capital gains rate; profit is taxable income at the income tax rates when residential property is sold within 2 years (bright-line, sales from 1 July 2024), when property or shares were bought mainly to resell, or in a dealing business or profit-making scheme. Paid by sellers. Income Tax Act 2007 (land sale and bright-line rules; ordinary income rules for shares).

source.title: Inland Revenue: The bright-line test

rows.label: Withholding on interest and dividends: resident and non-resident withholding tax [national]
rows.value: RWT on interest 10.5% to 39% by income (33% if no rate chosen, 45% without an IRD number); dividends 33%; NRWT 15% on interest and royalties and 30% on dividends where no double tax agreement applies. Paid by recipients (withheld by the payer). Income Tax Act 2007 (RWT and NRWT rules).
rows.note: Checklist item A6; detailed table: withholding-investment

source.title: Inland Revenue: Resident withholding tax (RWT)

rows.label: Rental income and pension income [national]
rows.value: Net rental income (gross rent less allowable expenses) taxed at the income tax rates; NZ Superannuation and foreign pensions are taxable income. Paid by landlords, including non-residents with New Zealand property, and pensioners. Income Tax Act 2007.
rows.note: Checklist item A7; detailed table: rental-income

source.title: Inland Revenue: Residential rental income and paying tax on it

rows.label: Excise duties on alcohol, tobacco and fuel [national]
rows.value: Excise duty on alcohol, tobacco and fuel made or stored in Customs-controlled areas, and excise-equivalent duty on imports (rates by product in the Tariff; not stored here). Paid by manufacturers and importers (passed on in prices). Customs and Excise Act 2018.

source.title: New Zealand Customs Service: Excise duty

rows.label: Inheritance, estate and gift tax [national]
rows.value: None: estate duty was abolished in 1992 and gift duty for gifts made on or after 1 October 2011. Paid by nobody. Estate and Gift Duties Act 1968 sections 2 and 61 as amended (gift duty abolition).

source.title: Inland Revenue, Policy Advice Division: Gift duty abolition, special report (1 September 2011)

rows.label: Departure levy: Customs border processing levy on travellers [national]
rows.value: NZ$3.62 plus GST per traveller departing by air or private boat (until 30 June 2027); NZ$25.07 on arrival by air (Customs and MPI biosecurity levies). Paid by travellers (usually included in the ticket). Border processing levy rates published in the New Zealand Gazette.

source.title: New Zealand Customs Service: Border processing levies

Paid by importers and travellers. Customs and Excise Act 2018; Tariff Act 1988; Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
